query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate during sliding in the high-temperature operating regime are governed by the activation of non-basal pyramidal 〈c + a〉 slip and deformation twinning in the epsilon phase, which is influenced by the c/a ratio and transformation volume change induced by alloying elements and processing conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate
generation.intervention: Controlled change in alloying elements and processing conditions to alter the c/a ratio and transformation volume change
generation.structural_mediator: Epsilon phase with non-basal pyramidal 〈c + a〉 slip and deformation twinning
generation.mechanism: Activation of non-basal pyramidal 〈c + a〉 slip and deformation twinning in the epsilon phase, influenced by the c/a ratio and transformation volume change
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance and reduced microscopic deformation
generation.baseline: Conventional metal substrate without high-entropy alloy coating
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between the c/a ratio, transformation volume change, and wear resistance is not fully understood and requires further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with controlled temperature and sliding conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating are not significantly improved compared to the conventional metal substrate without coating, the hypothesis is falsified.

Activation of different slip systems in hexagonal close packed (h.c.p.) metals depends primarily on the c/a ratio, which is an intrinsic property that can be altered through alloying addition. In conventional h.c.p. alloys where there is no diffusion-less phase transformation and associated transformation volume change with deformation, the c/a ratio remains constant during deformation. In the present study, c/a ratio and transformation volume change of h.c.p. epsilon martensite phase in transformative high entropy alloys (HEAs) were quantified as functions of alloy chemistry, friction stir processing and tensile deformation. The study revealed that while intrinsic c/a is dependent on alloying elements, c/a of epsilon in transformative HEAs changes with processing and deformation. This is attributed to transformation volume change induced dependence of h.c.p. lattice parameters on microstructure and stress state. Lower than ideal c/a ratio promotes non-basal pyramidal 〈c + a〉 slip and deformation twinning in epsilon phase of transformative HEAs.
